xs_si_mom_composite · how the strategy works, and how it did from 1 January 2025

The idea in one paragraph. Each day the strategy gives every one of the ~500 most traded US stocks two scores:
  • Short interest. How little short sellers bet against the stock: FINRA's days-to-cover. Few short sellers is good, a crowded short is bad.
  • Momentum. How steadily the stock beat what its market exposure explains over the past year, leaving out the last month.
It averages the two ranks. It buys the 15 best and sells short the 15 worst, with the same dollars on each side (45% of the account each). It holds each one until its rank falls back, and trades at the next day's open. Nothing in it was tuned. What this notebook shows, on real data from 2025-01-02 to the last bar in the database:
  1. The universe: which stocks can be picked, re-formed every six months.
  2. How one stock is scored, step by step: days-to-cover → its rank; one year of returns → its momentum rank; the two ranks → the combined rank → the book's entry and exit rules.
  3. The stock-picking assessment on any day you choose (the last day = what the strategy holds now): every eligible stock ranked, the 15 + 15 picks, and the orders for the next open.
  4. How the book performed against buying and holding the same universe, and against SPY.
  5. A timeline of every position: when it was opened and closed, its P&L and why it closed.
  6. One position up close: why it was bought, what it did, why it was sold.
Nothing here is tuned or selected: the rules are config.yaml as shipped. The first run reads the database (about 5 minutes); later runs read a cached copy in var/ (about 20 seconds).

0 · Load the data and run the strategy

  • Prices: daily bars, split- and dividend-adjusted, from 2022. Momentum needs about two years of history before the first traded day.
  • Short interest: FINRA's days-to-cover, usable the day after FINRA publishes it.
  • Share counts: SEC filings, used for the "too crowded to short" cap and the borrow fee.
  • The universe: the 500 most traded stocks, re-formed every six months.
  • The account: its size only scales the dollar figures; the returns do not depend on it. $33,000 gives the 30 positions of about $1,000 that the cost model prices: $0.005 a share, at least $1, plus 3 bp of spread and slippage.

Loaded:
  • 619 stocks (every name that was ever in the universe);
  • prices 2022-01-03 → 2026-10-16;
  • the newest short-interest value on 2026-10-16;
  • the book traded from 2025-01-02: 88 positions.
Engine messages: none. The last price bar is the newest the database holds. Refresh prices and short interest (notebooks/03_altdata_update.py, tsim backfill) before reading §3 as today's picks.

1 · The universe: which stocks can be picked

Formation. Every six months (1 January and 1 July) the universe is re-formed from the six months before:
  • the 500 stocks with the highest median daily dollar volume;
  • with a median price of at least $5, at least $50M traded a day and at least 100 sessions;
  • common stocks only, so ETFs are left out.
Point in time. A stock counts only while it is a member. When it drops out at a re-formation, the strategy sells (or covers) it at the next open. Eligible on a given day. A member is eligible when, that day:
  • it closed at $5 or more;
  • FINRA has a days-to-cover for it (masked once it is 45 days old);
  • SEC has a share count.
Only eligible stocks are ranked.

data.text/markdown:
2 · How one stock is scored

Pick a stock: the list holds every stock the strategy traded, biggest P&L first. The three charts below follow it through the strategy's three steps:
  1. its short-interest rank;
  2. its momentum rank;
  3. its combined rank and the book's entry and exit rules.

Step 1 · Short interest → the short-interest rank

  • Days-to-cover = shares sold short ÷ the average daily volume: how many days of normal trading the short sellers would need to buy their shares back. FINRA publishes it twice a month, so it moves in steps.
  • The strategy averages it over the last 42 sessions, about two months, so one report does not jump the score.
  • It then ranks that average against the other eligible stocks of similar liquidity: five dollar-volume groups, so a giant is not compared with a small cap.
  • Low days-to-cover gets a high rank (close to 1): short sellers avoid the stock, which is good for a long. High days-to-cover gets a low rank (close to 0): a crowded short.

data.text/markdown:
Step 2 · One year of returns → the momentum rank

Raw momentum ("it went up") is mostly the market. The strategy uses residual momentum:
  1. The market part. Each day's return of the stock minus β × the equal-weight market's return, with β the stock's sensitivity to the market over the last 252 sessions. What is left (the residual) is the part the market cannot explain.
  2. The window. The residuals are summed over months t−12 … t−1. The last month is skipped: last month's winners tend to give some back.
  3. The score. The sum is divided by the residuals' standard deviation, so a steady climb scores higher than one lucky jump.
  4. The rank. On the last session of each month every eligible stock is ranked on that score (1 = the strongest), and the rank holds for the whole next month.
Choose a month-end to see the calculation behind that month's rank.

<li><strong>This month-end.</strong> The residual over the scored eleven months summed to

<li><strong>The score and rank.</strong> The score is that sum divided by the standard deviation:

  dot).</li>
<li><strong>The shading.</strong> The grey band is the skipped last month. The light purple band is the
  month that uses this rank: it starts at the chosen month-end and runs to the next one.</li>
<li><strong>One time axis.</strong> Both charts share it, so each step in the purple line sits under the

Step 3 · The combined rank, and when the stock is bought or sold

  1. The combined rank = the average of the two ranks (a missing rank counts as 0.5), averaged over the last 5 sessions and ranked again among the eligible stocks.
  2. A long enters when its combined rank reaches 0.90 (the top 10%) and a long slot is free; with more candidates than slots, the best go first. It leaves when the rank falls below 0.80.
  3. A short enters at 0.10 or below (the bottom 10%) and leaves above 0.20.
  4. Other exits:
    • after 126 sessions without the rank returning to its entry zone;
    • a short that rises 100% from its entry (the squeeze stop);
    • a short whose short interest exceeds 30% of its shares (too crowded to borrow);
    • a stock that leaves the universe or loses its data.

    • every decision is made at the close and filled at the next open;
    • 15 longs and 15 shorts of 3% of the account each, sized at that open;
    • a long that grows to 6% (twice its slot) is trimmed back to 3%.

3 · The stock-picking assessment on one day

This is the whole decision the strategy makes at one close.
  • Choose a day: the default is the last bar, i.e. what the strategy holds now and what it would trade at the next open.
  • Every eligible stock gets its two ranks and its combined rank.
  • The 15 + 15 picks: the 15 longs and 15 shorts are the stocks inside the bands that won a slot, and positions already held keep their slots.

data.text/markdown:
4 · How the book performed

The comparisons:
  • Equal-weight buy-and-hold of the same universe: at each re-formation it buys every member equally and holds until the next one. It pays no costs.
  • SPY.
Two numbers matter:
  • Beta is how much of the market's move the book carries. Long and short in equal dollars still leaves some.
  • Alpha is the yearly return left after that market exposure: CAGR − beta × the benchmark's CAGR. It is what the stock picking earned.

data.text/html:
Reading it:
  • The strategy compounded +13.6% a year, carried a beta of 0.34 to the universe, and earned an alpha of +8.0% a year.
  • Its worst drawdown was -18.2%.
  • A market-neutral book is not built to beat buy-and-hold in a rising market. Its job is to earn the alpha whatever the market does.

5 · Every position on a timeline

Each bar is one position, from the open it was bought (or sold short) at to the open it was closed at. Positions still held run to the last bar.
  • Color is the result: green made money, red lost money. Solid bars are longs, hatched bars shorts.
  • Hover a bar for its prices, its P&L, its ranks and why it closed.

7 · What to keep in mind

  • This is one continuous book. The research (PROPOSALS_RESULTS.md) restarted the book every half-year and measured it on four groups of stocks. This notebook runs one book from 2025-01-02 on, as a live account would, so its numbers differ somewhat from the research tables.
  • The benchmark is point in time. It buys the universe as it stood at each re-formation. An equal-weight buy-and-hold of every name in the panel would include stocks that only joined in 2026 because they had risen: look-ahead.
  • Fills are at the next open, with modelled costs and borrow. Every recent short was borrowable at IBKR, mostly at 0.3-0.4% a year. A few business development companies cost 3-9%.
  • The "too crowded to short" cap inherits a known flaw from informed_flow_ls v6. It reads short interest ÷ shares with a volume that is split-adjusted backward. Before a forward split that overstates the ratio, so a stock about to split can be kept out of the short book: a small look-ahead. informed_flow_ls v8 fixed it in its own code; here it touches the cap and the borrow tier, never the ranks.
  • The database holds only stocks that still exist (survivors), which flatters the long side and the benchmark.
  • On the top 500 the book has carried net market exposure since mid-2025 (rolling beta, §4). See TOP_STRATEGIES.md §4 for the market hedge.
